question: Should OpenClaw accept `tools.exec.denylist` plus `exec-approvals.json` denylist fields as a permanent human-only, deny-over-allow policy overriding `security=full` and `ask=off`?
rationale: The feature changes command authorization and establishes two persisted configuration and protocol contracts; technical correctness cannot decide that permanent policy.

options.title: Accept both layers safely
options.body: Integrate both denylist sources into the current runtime and persisted-policy checkpoints while preserving one-shot human approval.

options.title: Approvals file only
options.body: Remove `tools.exec.denylist` and retain the host approvals-file policy under its existing transaction boundary.

options.title: Reject deny-by-exception
options.body: Retain the existing deny, allowlist, and full modes without this policy.

recommendation.title: Accept both layers safely
recommendation.body: Integrate both denylist sources into the current runtime and persisted-policy checkpoints while preserving one-shot human approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged commits own the canonical exec-approval transaction and delayed-policy revocation contract.
